correctness.rationale: Polar vertex characterization follows from tight-edge connectedness: with hub potential zero each clique blade has one chosen sign on a nonempty subset and zeros elsewhere, giving all and only extreme potentials. A centered polar normal from k nonzero leaves and signed sum s has norm²=k−s²/(a+b+1). Opposite signs dominate equal signs; all a smaller-blade leaves must be active; the remaining t in larger blade maximizes Q(t)=a+t−(t−a)²/N. Completing the square gives α=(3a+b+1)/2, exact discrete tie thresholds, contact multiplicities and sharp parity. Central symmetry converts origin-centered inradius to global radius. The span of contact normals has ranks 1, b or b+1, so its orthogonal complement gives all incenter affine dimensions with strict noncontact slack. Independent exact-rational enumeration checked 40,396 patterns in bounded parameters, not all integers.
